text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government opens crossing point between Sidon and Jezzine after a 12-year closure. Jezzine, officially outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, is under control of Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army militia.

- The Independent: Bombs of "Grapes of Wrath" were taken from U.S. army arsenal immediately before Israel launched 17-day blitz against Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon in 1996, killing about 200 people -- mostly women and children.
- Japanese diplomat meets Prime Minister Hariri and Foreign Minister Bouez: peace process is in danger and Israel must restart talks.
- Balance of payments registers $47.5 million deficit at end of April.
- Net public debt at 17,949 billion Lebanese pounds at end of April.
- Saudi grants and loans to Lebanon total $530 million.
- Public utilities workers suspend strike planned for Wednesday.
- Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah in Lebanon on Thursday with 162-member delegation.
- U.S. semi-official delegation to Jordan, Syria and Lebanon on June 28. Partial lifting as of July of travel ban on American businessmen and those of Arab origins.
- Israel's local militia allies in south Lebanon receive advanced arms from Jewish state.
